questions.prompt: What is study doing in this chapter?
choices: Acting as passive time near the material
Acting as active processing that tests understanding
Replacing the need for focus

explanation.gentle: Yes. The chapter treats study as active work on the material.
explanation.direct: Study here means interacting with the material in ways that reveal and strengthen understanding.
explanation.competitive: It is making the rep answer, not hovering near it.

questions.prompt: Why is familiarity not enough in this chapter?
choices: Because recognizable material may still be weak, unusable, or hard to retrieve
Because familiarity is always useless
Because only memory matters once material looks known

explanation.gentle: Right. The chapter keeps separating recognition from deeper understanding.
explanation.direct: Material can look known before it becomes retrievable, usable, or well integrated.
explanation.competitive: A friendly-looking rep can still fold under demand.

questions.prompt: A learner keeps rereading the same material until it feels known. What would Chapter 12 most likely say?
choices: That this alone proves mastery
That stronger study asks the learner to do something active with the material
That passive exposure is the strongest study method

explanation.gentle: The chapter wants more than repeated exposure.
explanation.direct: Better study makes the learner retrieve, restate, question, connect, or otherwise work the material.
explanation.competitive: Stop petting the rep and make it answer.

questions.prompt: Priya is choosing between rereading highlighted pages and restating the core idea without looking. What fits Chapter 12?
choices: Choose the move that gives stronger evidence of understanding
Choose the smoother move because comfort means learning
Stay with the page until it feels familiar enough

explanation.gentle: Yes. The chapter favors active proof over passive comfort.
explanation.direct: Priya should pick the action that reveals whether understanding is really present.

That repeated exposure created familiarity without equally strong learning
That time on the material always guarantees retention

explanation.gentle: Exactly. The chapter treats this as a familiarity trap.
explanation.direct: Mateo sees that the material stayed recognizable without becoming sturdy or usable enough.

questions.prompt: Which statement would Chapter 12 reject as a misreading?
choices: Active interaction can improve study quality
Familiarity is the same thing as mastery
Study uses attention better when it does more than passive review

explanation.gentle: Correct. The chapter keeps warning that familiarity can mislead.
explanation.direct: Recognition is weaker evidence than retrieval, reconstruction, or usable explanation.
explanation.competitive: A smiling rep is not the same as a strong one.

questions.prompt: Why can active processing improve learning quality?
choices: Because it forces understanding to reveal itself more honestly
Because it removes all effort from studying
Because it makes every subject identical

explanation.gentle: Yes. The chapter values actions that expose whether learning is real.
explanation.direct: Active study strengthens learning because the material has to be retrieved, tested, or worked instead of merely revisited.
explanation.competitive: Pressure tells the truth about the rep.

questions.prompt: Jordan’s understanding gets sharper before confidence rises when review becomes active. What does that show?
choices: That active study can improve clarity before it feels comfortable or impressive
That confidence no longer matters at all
That active review only works in tutoring centers

explanation.gentle: The chapter expects stronger evidence before stronger feeling.
explanation.direct: Active processing can sharpen understanding before confidence noticeably catches up.
explanation.competitive: The rep got honest before it got flattering.

questions.prompt: What tension does the chapter protect most carefully?
choices: How to study actively without turning the session into frantic technique theater
How to make passive review the enemy in every context
How to replace memory with study method entirely

explanation.gentle: Right. The chapter wants better study without decorative method mania.
explanation.direct: Its guardrail is that active processing matters, but study should still stay practical rather than theatrical.
explanation.competitive: Work the rep hard without cosplaying brilliance around it.

questions.prompt: How does Chapter 12 prepare the next chapter?
choices: It completes memory in advance
It deepens the learning encounter so the next question becomes how to retain and retrieve it
It proves study matters more than every other method

explanation.gentle: Yes. Once study becomes active, memory becomes the next practical question.
explanation.direct: The chapter bridges into memory by asking how what was actively worked can later be kept and retrieved.
explanation.competitive: Make the rep real first, then ask how to keep it.
